q: All praise belongs to Allaah Who created the heavens and the earth and Who made multitudes
Then too the Kuffaar make equals with
v.s: [All] praise is [due] to God, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darkness and the light. Then those who disbelieve equate [others] with their Lord.
v.c: All praise is for Allah Who created the heavens and the earth and made darkness and light. Yet the disbelievers set up equals to their Lord ˹in worship˺.

q: He is the One Who created you
from clay and then fixed a term
(resurrection, little realising that the Being Who can create you from sand can certainly resurrect you again)!
v.s: It is He who created you from clay and then decreed a term and a specified time [known] to Him; then [still] you are in dispute.
v.c: He is the One Who created you from clay, then appointed a term ˹for your death˺ and another known only to Him ˹for your resurrection˺ —yet you continue to doubt!

q: (Who is The Only One deserving to be worshipped)
in the heavens and in the earth. He knows your secrets and what you make known and He knows what you earn
(whatever actions you do, so act in accordance with the Shari'ah).
v.s: And He is God, [the only deity] in the heavens and the earth. He knows your secret and what you make public, and He knows that which you earn.
v.c: He is the Only True God in the heavens and the earth. He knows whatever you conceal and whatever you reveal, and knows whatever you do.

q: of their Rabb comes to them
v.s: And no sign comes to them from the signs of their Lord except that they turn away therefrom.
v.c: Whenever a sign comes to them from their Lord, they turn away from it.

q: have denied the truth when it came to them. Soon the news
of what they mocked shall come to them
(and they will regret what they did).
v.s: For they had denied the truth when it came to them, but there is going to reach them the news of what they used to ridicule.
v.c: They have indeed rejected the truth when it came to them, so they will soon face the consequences of their ridicule.

q: (the Kuffaar like the Aad and Thamud)
(as they passed the ruins of past nations on their journeys)
how many nations We have destroyed before them, whom We had established on earth as We have not established you
(We had given them more might and resources than We have given you)? (Although)
We sent to them abundant rains and made rivers flow beneath them
(because of which they were very prosperous),
because of their sins and created other nations after them.
v.s: Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them which We had established upon the earth as We have not established you? And We sent [rain from] the sky upon them in showers and made rivers flow beneath them; then We destroyed them for their sins and brought forth after them a generation of others.
v.c: Have they not seen how many ˹disbelieving˺ peoples We destroyed before them? We had made them more established in the land than you. We sent down abundant rain for them and made rivers flow at their feet. Then We destroyed them for their sins and replaced them with other peoples.

q: say, “This is nothing less than obvious magic.”
v.s: And even if We had sent down to you, [O Muhammad], a written scripture on a page and they touched it with their hands, the disbelievers would say, “This is not but obvious magic.”
v.c: Had We sent down to you ˹O Prophet˺ a revelation in writing and they were to touch it with their own hands, the disbelievers would still have said, “This is nothing but pure magic!”

m: respite would have been granted to them
q: say, “Why is an angel not sent to him
(to Muhammad ﷺ to verify that he is a prophet)?”
If We were to send an angel
(as they request and if they still refuse to accept that he is a Prophet),
will be decided and then they
v.s: And they say, "Why was there not sent down to him an angel?" But if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided; then they would not be reprieved.
v.c: They say, “Why has no ˹visible˺ angel come with him?” Had We sent down an angel, the matter would have certainly been settled ˹at once˺, and they would have never been given more time ˹to repent˺.

q: If We were to make him
(as the Kuffaar request when they say that the Prophets are nothing more than human beings like themselves and should rather have been angels),
(because humans cannot see an angel in his true form)
and then cast the same doubt on them in which they find themselves
(they would then again say that the Prophet is merely a human being like themselves).
v.s: And if We had made him [i.e., the messenger] an angel, We would have made him [appear as] a man, and We would have covered them with that in which they cover themselves [i.e., confusion and doubt].
v.c: And if We had sent an angel, We would have certainly made it ˹assume the form of˺ a man—leaving them more confused than they already are.

q: Indeed Rusul before you were also mocked, then those who mocked were surrounded by
that which they used to mock.
v.s: And already were messengers ridiculed before you, but those who mocked them were enveloped by that which they used to ridicule.
v.c: ˹Other˺ messengers had already been ridiculed before you ˹O Prophet˺, but those who mocked them were overtaken by what they used to ridicule.

q: (by seeing the ruins of previous nations,)
(the message of their Prophets. In this manner you will learn from their experiences and will not repeat their mistakes).'
v.s: Say, "Travel through the land; then observe how was the end of the deniers."
v.c: Say, “Travel throughout the land and see the fate of the deniers.”

q: Say, “To whom belongs everything in the heavens and earth?” Say
(because of which He does not punish people immediately).
He will certainly gather you all on the Day of Qiyaamah about which there is no doubt. Those who have cast
(those who are destined to be destroyed)
v.s: Say, "To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth?" Say, "To God." He has decreed upon Himself mercy. He will surely assemble you for the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt. Those who will lose themselves [that Day] do not believe.
v.c: Ask ˹them, O Prophet˺, “To whom belongs everything in the heavens and the earth?” Say, “To Allah!” He has taken upon Himself to be Merciful. He will certainly gather ˹all of˺ you together for the Day of Judgment— about which there is no doubt. But those who have ruined themselves will never believe.

q: To Him belongs whatever lies still
(Allaah is the Creator and Master of everything).
(hears everything in the noise of the day and in the silence of the night),
(knows and attends to the needs of all).
v.s: And to Him belongs that which reposes by night and by day, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
v.c: To Him belongs whatever exists in the day and night. And He is the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.

q: Say, “Should I take as a helper anyone else besides Allaah Who has created the heavens and the earth and Who feeds
(all need Him while He needs none)?”
“Verily I have been commanded to be the first Muslim
(to be the first to submit to Allaah's obedience)
and not to be of the Mushrikeen.”
v.s: Say, “Is it other than God I should take as a protector, Creator of the heavens and earth, while it is He who feeds and is not fed?” Say, [O Muhammad], “Indeed, I have been commanded to be the first [among you] who submit [to God] and [was commanded], ‘Do not ever be of the polytheists.’”
v.c: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Will I take any guardian other than Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, Who provides for all and is not in need of provision?” Say, “I have been commanded to be the first to submit and not be one of the polytheists.”

q: fear the punishment of a tremendous day
(the Day of Qiyaamah because no one is above the divine law).”
v.s: Say, "Indeed I fear, if I should disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day."
v.c: Say, “I truly fear—if I were to disobey my Lord—the torment of a tremendous Day.”

q: Allaah is indeed merciful to the one from whom punishment is averted
v.s: He from whom it is averted that Day - [God] has granted him mercy. And that is the clear attainment.
v.c: Whoever is spared the torment of that Day will have certainly been shown Allah’s mercy. And that is the absolute triumph.

q: you with harm, there shall be none
If He grants you good, then He has power over all things
(and none can take the good away from you).
v.s: And if God should touch you with adversity, there is no remover of it except Him. And if He touches you with good - then He is over all things competent.
v.c: If Allah touches you with harm, none can undo it except Him. And if He touches you with a blessing, He is Most Capable of everything.

q: over His bondmen and He is the Wise, the Informed.
v.s: And He is the subjugator over His servants. And He is the Wise, the Acquainted [with all].
v.c: He reigns supreme over His creation. And He is the All-Wise, All-Aware.

q: (to the truth of Rasulullaah ﷺ and Islaam)?”
He is the Witness between myself and yourselves. This Qur'aan has been revealed to me so that I may warn you with it as well as
really bear witness that there are other gods with Allaah?” Say
is but One Ilaah and I am certainly
(I openly express my aversion to all types of Shirk).”
v.s: Say, "What thing is greatest in testimony?" Say, "God is witness between me and you. And this Qur’ān was revealed to me that I may warn you thereby and whomever it reaches. Do you [truly] testify that with God there are other deities?" Say, "I will not testify [with you]." Say, "Indeed, He is but one God, and indeed, I am free of what you associate [with Him]."
v.c: Ask ˹them, O Prophet˺, “Who is the best witness?” Say, “Allah is! He is a Witness between me and you. And this Quran has been revealed to me so that, with it, I may warn you and whoever it reaches. Do you ˹pagans˺ testify that there are other gods besides Allah?” ˹Then˺ say, “I will never testify ˹to this˺!” ˹And˺ say, “There is only One God. And I totally reject whatever ˹idols˺ you associate with Him.”

q: Those who have been given the Book
like they recognise their own children
(because of his description in their scriptures).
(because of their malice, pride, love for wealth, love for power, hide the truth)
have cast their souls to destruction
because they will not accept Imaan.
v.s: Those to whom We have given the Scripture recognize it as they recognize their [own] sons. Those who will lose themselves [in the Hereafter] do not believe.
v.c: Those to whom We gave the Scripture recognize him ˹to be a true prophet˺ as they recognize their own children. Those who have ruined themselves will never believe.

q: Who can be more unjust than he who invents lies against Allaah
and rejects His Aayaat? Surely, the unjust ones
v.s: And who is more unjust than one who invents about God a lie or denies His verses? Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.
v.c: Who does more wrong than those who fabricate lies against Allah or deny His signs? Indeed, the wrongdoers will never succeed.

q: The day when We shall gather them all together and then ask those who committed Shirk
v.s: And [mention, O Muhammad], the Day We will gather them all together; then We will say to those who associated others with God, “Where are your ‘partners’ that you used to claim [with Him]?”
v.c: ˹Consider˺ the Day We will gather them all together then ask those who associated others ˹with Allah in worship˺, “Where are those gods you used to claim?”

q: then will be to swear, “By Allaah our Rabb, we never committed Shirk!”
v.s: Then there will be no [excuse upon] examination except they will say, "By God, our Lord, we were not those who associated."
v.c: Their only argument will be: “By Allah, our Lord! We were never polytheists.”

q: See how they lie against themselves! That which they fabricated
(in the Aakhirah and unable to help them in the least).
v.s: See how they will lie about themselves. And lost from them will be what they used to invent.
v.c: See how they will lie about themselves and how those ˹gods˺ they fabricated will fail them!

q: are those who listen attentively to you
(O Muhammad ﷺ when you recite the Qur'aan). (However)
We have placed a veil on their hearts lest they should understand, and in their ears is a deafness
(so that they do not hear with the intention of accepting).
Even if they see every Aayah, they will not believe in it; to the point that the Kuffaar will
with you saying, “This (Qur'aan) is merely fables
v.s: And among them are those who listen to you, but We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness. And if they should see every sign, they will not believe in it. Even when they come to you arguing with you, those who disbelieve say, "This is not but legends of the former peoples."
v.c: There are some of them who ˹pretend to˺ listen to your recitation ˹of the Quran˺, but We have cast veils over their hearts—leaving them unable to comprehend it—and deafness in their ears. Even if they were to see every sign, they still would not believe in them. The disbelievers would ˹even˺ come to argue with you, saying, “This ˹Quran˺ is nothing but ancient fables!”

q: (from the Qur'aan and from following Rasulullaah ﷺ)
and they themselves avoid it. They destroy only themselves
(by doing this because they will suffer the punishment for it),
but they take no notice of it
v.s: And they prevent [others] from him and are [themselves] remote from him. And they do not destroy except themselves, but they perceive [it] not.
v.c: They turn others away from the Prophet and distance themselves as well. They ruin none but themselves, yet they fail to perceive it.

q: when they will be made to stand over the Fire
and they will say, “O dear! If only we could be returned
we would not reject the Aayaat of our Rabb and we would be from among the Mu'mineen!”
v.s: If you could but see when they are made to stand before the Fire and will say, "Oh, would that we could be returned [to life on earth] and not deny the signs of our Lord and be among the believers."
v.c: If only you could see when they will be detained before the Fire! They will cry, “Oh! If only we could be sent back, we would never deny the signs of our Lord and we would ˹surely˺ be of the believers.”

q: If they were to be sent back
return to what had been prohibited to them
(because they will not fulfil their promise to be Mu'mineen if ever they were returned to the world).
v.s: But what they concealed before has [now] appeared to them. And even if they were returned, they would return to that which they were forbidden; and indeed, they are liars.
v.c: But no! ˹They only say this˺ because the truth they used to hide will become all too clear to them. Even if they were to be sent back, they would certainly revert to what they were forbidden. Indeed they are liars!

q: say, “This is merely our worldly life
(to enjoy, so eat, drink and be merry)
and we will not be raised
v.s: And they say, "There is none but our worldly life, and we will not be resurrected."
v.c: They insisted, “There is nothing beyond this worldly life and we will never be resurrected.”

m: they will be made to stand
q: when they will be made to stand
before their Rabb. He will say, “Is this
They will reply, “Indeed, by our Rabb!” He will tell them, “Taste the punishment because you committed kufr
v.s: If you could but see when they will be made to stand before their Lord. He will say, “Is this not the truth?” They will say, “Yes, by our Lord.” He will [then] say, “So taste the punishment because you used to disbelieve.”
v.c: But if only you could see when they will be detained before their Lord! He will ask ˹them˺, “Is this ˹Hereafter˺ not the truth?” They will cry, “Absolutely, by our Lord!” He will say, “Then taste the punishment for your disbelief.”

q: who deny meeting with Allaah until, when the Hour
suddenly comes and they cry out, “O dear! How much do we regret our negligence
in the world!” They will bear the burden
of their sins on their backs. Alas! Evil indeed is that which they bear
(because it will be the cause of terrible punishment for them).
v.s: Those will have lost who deny the meeting with God, until when the Hour [of resurrection] comes upon them unexpectedly, they will say, "Oh, [how great is] our regret over what we neglected concerning it [i.e., the Hour]," while they bear their burdens [i.e., sins] on their backs. Unquestionably, evil is that which they bear.
v.c: Losers indeed are those who deny the meeting with Allah until the Hour takes them by surprise, then they will cry, “Woe to us for having ignored this!” They will bear ˹the burden of˺ their sins on their backs. Evil indeed is their burden!

q: (besides those things done to please Allaah)
and sport and most certainly the home of the Aakhirah is best for those with Taqwa
(those who realise that the Aakhirah is their true home).
v.s: And the worldly life is not but amusement and diversion; but the home of the Hereafter is best for those who fear God, so will you not reason?
v.c: This worldly life is no more than play and amusement, but far better is the ˹eternal˺ Home of the Hereafter for those mindful ˹of Allah˺. Will you not then understand?

q: We know well that their talks
grieve you. Indeed they do not reject you
(they do not regard you as a liar because they know that you are not one),
but these oppressors deny the Aayaat of Allaah.
v.s: We know that you, [O Muhammad], are saddened by what they say. And indeed, they do not call you untruthful, but it is the verses of God that the wrongdoers reject.
v.c: We certainly know that what they say grieves you ˹O Prophet˺. It is not your honesty they question—it is Allah’s signs that the wrongdoers deny.

q: Without doubt, many Rusul before you were rejected
but they bore the rejection with patience and they were harassed until Our assistance
(Therefore, you should exercise patience until Our assistance reaches you).
There is none to alter the words
of Allaah. Some narratives of the Ambiyaa have certainly come to you
(by which you may be encouraged and by which your heart may be put at ease).
v.s: And certainly were messengers denied before you, but they were patient over [the effects of] denial, and they were harmed until Our victory came to them. And none can alter the words [i.e., decrees] of God. And there has certainly come to you some information about the [previous] messengers.
v.c: Indeed, messengers before you were rejected but patiently endured rejection and persecution until Our help came to them. And Allah’s promise ˹to help˺ is never broken. And you have already received some of the narratives of these messengers.

m: so that you bring to them
q: then, if you are able to do so, search for a tunnel
into the earth or a ladder to the sky and bring forth a miracle for them
(since you cannot do this, you will have to exercise patience until Allaah deals with them).
If Allaah willed, He would have gathered them all upon guidance
(but, He did not desire to do so).
So do not be of the uninformed ones
v.s: And if their evasion is difficult for you, then if you are able to seek a tunnel into the earth or a stairway into the sky to bring them a sign, [then do so]. But if God had willed, He would have united them upon guidance. So never be of the ignorant.
v.c: If you find their denial unbearable, then build—if you can—a tunnel through the earth or stairs to the sky to bring them a ˹more compelling˺ sign. Had Allah so willed, He could have guided them all. So do not be one of those ignorant ˹of this fact˺.

q: (to you with the intention of believing)
(your call to Imaan. Do not expect everyone to accept Imaan).
(those who do not listen with the intention of accepting),
and then they will be returned to Him
v.s: Only those who hear will respond. But the dead - God will resurrect them; then to Him they will be returned.
v.c: Only the attentive will respond ˹to your call˺. As for the dead, Allah will raise them up, then to Him they will ˹all˺ be returned.

q: from his Rabb?” Say, “Verily Allaah is able to send a sign
but most of them do not know
(that seeing a miracle is not always good because they will be almost immediately destroyed if they refuse to believe the miracle).'
v.s: And they say, "Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?" Say, "Indeed, God is Able to send down a sign, but most of them do not know."
v.c: They ask, “Why has no ˹other˺ sign been sent down to him from his Lord?” Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Allah certainly has the power to send down a sign”—though most of them do not know.

q: Every creature on the earth and every bird flying with its two wings are nations
(because Allaah has also predestined their sustenance and their experiences).
(after passing their lives in this world)
shall be gathered to their Rabb
(on the Day of Qiyaamah when even oppressive animals will be made to pay for their oppression).
v.s: And there is no creature on [or within] the earth or bird that flies with its wings except [that they are] communities like you. We have not neglected in the Register a thing. Then unto their Lord they will be gathered.
v.c: All living beings roaming the earth and winged birds soaring in the sky are communities like yourselves. We have left nothing out of the Record. Then to their Lord they will be gathered all together.

q: Those who deny Our Aayaat are deaf and dumb
(unable to hear and see the truth and lost)
in a multitude of darkness. Allaah sends astray whom He wills and He shall place whom He wills on the straight path
v.s: But those who deny Our verses are deaf and dumb within darknesses. Whomever God wills - He leaves astray; and whomever He wills - He puts him on a straight path.
v.c: Those who deny Our signs are ˹wilfully˺ deaf and dumb—lost in darkness. Allah leaves whoever He wills to stray and guides whoever He wills to the Straight Way.

q: “Tell me, if Allaah's punishment has to strike you or if the Hour
has to dawn upon you, will you then call any
besides Allaah if you are truthful?”
(If you are truthful, will you admit that you can call on none but Allaah to assist you?)
v.s: Say, "Have you considered: if there came to you the punishment of God or there came to you the Hour - is it other than God you would invoke, if you should be truthful?"
v.c: Ask ˹them, O Prophet˺, “Imagine if you were overwhelmed by Allah’s torment or the Hour—would you call upon any other than Allah ˹for help˺? ˹Answer me˺ if your claims are true!

q: No, you will call only for Him
and, if He wills, He will remove the calamity
for which you call Him, after which you will forget those
v.s: No, it is Him [alone] you would invoke, and He would remove that for which you invoked Him if He willed, and you would forget what you associate [with Him].
v.c: No! He is the only One you would call. And if He willed, He could remove the affliction that made you invoke Him. Only then will you forget whatever you associate with Him ˹in worship˺.”

q: (when the people rejected the Ambiyaa and their message)
so that they may humble themselves
(and accept the message of the prophets).
v.s: And We have already sent [messengers] to nations before you, [O Muhammad]; then We seized them with poverty and hardship that perhaps they might humble themselves [to Us].
v.c: Indeed, We have sent messengers before you ˹O Prophet˺ to other people who We put through suffering and adversity ˹for their denial˺, so perhaps they would be humbled.

q: Why was it then that they did not show humility when Our punishment afflicted them? Instead, their hearts hardened
v.s: Then why, when Our punishment came to them, did they not humble themselves? But their hearts became hardened, and Satan made attractive to them that which they were doing.
v.c: Why did they not humble themselves when We made them suffer? Instead, their hearts were hardened, and Satan made their misdeeds appealing to them.

q: When they forgot the advice given to them, We opened to them the doors to all
things. When the time came that they rejoiced over what was given to them, We suddenly gripped hold of them
(having no hope of ever recovering the bounties they lost).
v.s: So when they forgot that by which they had been reminded, We opened to them the doors of every [good] thing until, when they rejoiced in that which they were given, We seized them suddenly, and they were [then] in despair.
v.c: When they became oblivious to warnings, We showered them with everything they desired. But just as they became prideful of what they were given, We seized them by surprise, then they instantly fell into despair!

q: Thus the roots of the oppressive
All praise is for Allaah, the Rabb of the universe
(Who assisted His Ambiyaa and those who followed them to remove the tyrants and oppressors).
v.s: So the people that committed wrong were eliminated. And praise to God, Lord of the worlds.
v.c: So the wrongdoers were utterly uprooted. And all praise is for Allah—Lord of all worlds.

q: Say, “Tell me, if Allaah snatches away your hearing and your sight and seals your hearts, which Ilaah besides Allaah can restore them to you?” See how We explain to them the Aayaat
(proving that Allaah is the One and Only Ilaah),
v.s: Say, "Have you considered: if God should take away your hearing and your sight and set a seal upon your hearts, which deity other than God could bring them [back] to you?" Look how We diversify the verses; then they [still] turn away.
v.c: Ask ˹them, O Prophet˺, “Imagine if Allah were to take away your hearing or sight, or seal your hearts—who else other than Allah could restore it?” See ˹O Prophet˺ how We vary the signs, yet they still turn away.

q: Say, “Tell me, if Allaah's punishment afflicts you suddenly or openly
(it will certainly be only the wrong-doers who will suffer)?”
v.s: Say, "Have you considered: if the punishment of God should come to you unexpectedly or manifestly, will any be destroyed but the wrongdoing people?"
v.c: Ask, “Imagine if Allah’s punishment were to overwhelm you with or without warning—who would be destroyed other than the wrongdoers?”

q: We have sent the Ambiyaa only as carriers
(to warn people about the punishment in store for the Kuffaar).
So whoever has Imaan and reforms
v.s: And We send not the messengers except as bringers of good tidings and warners. So whoever believes and reforms - there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
v.c: We have sent messengers only as deliverers of good news and as warners. Whoever believes and does good, there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve.

q: As for those who reject Our Aayaat, punishment shall afflict them because they sin
v.s: But those who deny Our verses - the punishment will touch them for their defiant disobedience.
v.c: But those who deny Our signs will be afflicted with punishment for their rebelliousness.

q: “I do not say to you that I possess the treasures of Allaah
(from which I can give you whatever you want),
nor do I have knowledge of the unseen
nor have I told you that I am an angel
I follow only what has been revealed to me.” Say, “Can a blind person
be equal to the one who sees
(reflect about this and realise that you ought to bring Imaan into your hearts)?”
v.s: Say, [O Muhammad], “I do not tell you that I have the depositories [containing the provision] of God or that I know the unseen, nor do I tell you that I am an angel. I only follow what is revealed to me.” Say, “Is the blind equivalent to the seeing? Then will you not give thought?”
v.c: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “I do not say to you that I possess Allah’s treasuries or know the unseen, nor do I claim to be an angel. I only follow what is revealed to me.” Say, “Are those blind ˹to the truth˺ equal to those who can see? Will you not then reflect?”

q: to warn those who fear that they will be gathered before their Rabb without any helper
so that they may grow concerned
(about their plight and forsake all sins).
v.s: And warn by it [i.e., the Qur’ān] those who fear that they will be gathered before their Lord - for them besides Him will be no protector and no intercessor - that they might become righteous.
v.c: Warn with this ˹Quran˺ those who are awed by the prospect of being gathered before their Lord—when they will have no protector or intercessor besides Him—so perhaps they will be mindful ˹of Him˺.

m: So were you to send them away
q: (When some respectable Mushrikeen told Rasulullaah ﷺ that they will listen to him on condition that he removes the poor Sahabah ﵃ from his gathering, Allaah instructed Rasulullaah ﷺ saying,)
their Rabb morning and evening, seeking His pleasure. You are not accountable
(by doing this). (Since you have no knowledge of the inner conditions of their hearts, you have no reason to drive them out of your gatherings.)
v.s: And do not send away those who call upon their Lord morning and afternoon, seeking His countenance. Not upon you is anything of their account and not upon them is anything of your account. So were you to send them away, you would [then] be of the wrongdoers.
v.c: ˹O Prophet!˺ Do not dismiss those ˹poor believers˺ who invoke their Lord morning and evening, seeking His pleasure. You are not accountable for them whatsoever, nor are they accountable for you. So do not dismiss them, or you will be one of the wrongdoers.

q: (as these people do not wish to associate with those of lower social standing)
to test others so that they
the ones whom Allaah has blessed from among us
(by guiding them to Islaam instead of us)?”
Allaah knows well who the grateful ones are
(and Allaah shall guide then to the straight path regardless of their social standing).
v.s: And thus We have tried some of them through others that they [i.e., the disbelievers] might say, "Is it these whom God has favored among us?" Is not God most knowing of those who are grateful?
v.c: In this way We have tested some by means of others, so those ˹disbelievers˺ may say, “Has Allah favoured these ˹poor believers˺ out of all of us?” Does Allah not best recognize the grateful?

q: When those who believe in Our Aayaat come to you, then say to them, “Peace be upon you. Your Rabb has made mercy
compulsory upon Himself. The fact is that whichever one of you sins out of ignorance
(all sins are committed out of ignorance because no person will sin if he really knows the punishment for the sin)
Allaah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful
v.s: And when those come to you who believe in Our verses, say, "Peace be upon you. Your Lord has decreed upon Himself mercy: that any of you who does wrong out of ignorance and then repents after that and corrects himself - indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful."
v.c: When the believers in Our revelations come to you, say, “Peace be upon you! Your Lord has taken upon Himself to be Merciful. Whoever among you commits evil ignorantly ˹or recklessly˺ then repents afterwards and mends their ways, then Allah is truly All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”

q: We clarify Aayaat so that the path
(and people may be able to stay away from this misleading path).
v.s: And thus do We detail the verses, and [thus] the way of the criminals will become evident.
v.c: This is how We make Our signs clear, so the way of the wicked may become distinct.

q: besides Allaah.” Say, “I do not follow your wishes
(and will not worship what you want me to worship),
for then I shall go astray and will not be of the rightly guided ones.”
v.s: Say, "Indeed, I have been forbidden to worship those you invoke besides God." Say, "I will not follow your desires, for I would then have gone astray, and I would not be of the [rightly] guided."
v.c: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “I have been forbidden to worship those you invoke besides Allah.” Say, “I will not follow your desires, for I then would certainly be astray and not one of those ˹rightly˺ guided.”

q: “Verily I am on a clear proof
from my Rabb, whereas you have rejected Him
which you seek to hasten. Decisions
(and He will decide whether to and when to punish).
the truth and is the best of all those who make decisions.”
v.s: Say, "Indeed, I am on clear evidence from my Lord, and you have denied it. I do not have that for which you are impatient. The decision is only for God. He relates the truth, and He is the best of deciders."
v.c: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Indeed, I stand on a clear proof from my Lord—yet you have denied it. That ˹torment˺ you seek to hasten is not within my power. It is only Allah Who decides ˹its time˺. He declares the truth. And He is the Best of Judges.”

q: you seek to hasten, the matter would have been decided between us
(because I would have allowed the punishment to destroy you a long time ago to be rid of your harassment). (However)
Allaah knows best who the oppressors
(and He will punish them whenever He decides).”
v.s: Say, "If I had that for which you are impatient, the matter would have been decided between me and you, but God is most knowing of the wrongdoers."
v.c: Say ˹also˺, “If what you seek to hasten were within my power, the matter between us would have already been settled. But Allah knows the wrongdoers best.”

q: of the unseen, about which none besides Him has any knowledge
He knows what is on the land and within the oceans. He is
Aware of every leaf falling from a tree. Every grain in the darkness of the earth and every moist and dry thing is
v.s: And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him. And He knows what is on the land and in the sea. Not a leaf falls but that He knows it. And no grain is there within the darknesses of the earth and no moist or dry [thing] but that it is [written] in a clear record.
v.c: With Him are the keys of the unseen—no one knows them except Him. And He knows what is in the land and sea. Not even a leaf falls without His knowledge, nor a grain in the darkness of the earth or anything—green or dry—but is ˹written˺ in a perfect Record.

q: He is the One Who raises your souls
knows what you do by day and awakens you
to Him is your return and He shall inform you of
v.s: And it is He who takes your souls by night and knows what you have committed by day. Then He revives you therein [i.e., by day] that a specified term may be fulfilled. Then to Him will be your return; then He will inform you about what you used to do.
v.c: He is the One Who calls back your souls by night and knows what you do by day, then revives you daily to complete your appointed term. To Him is your ˹ultimate˺ return, then He will inform you of what you used to do.
v.h: Sleep: The Twin Brother of Death

q: over His bondsmen and sends guardians
(some to protect you from calamities and others to record all your deeds)
until the time comes when death overtakes any of you. Then Our messengers
v.s: And He is the subjugator over His servants, and He sends over you guardian-angels until, when death comes to one of you, Our messengers [i.e., angles of death] take him, and they do not fail [in their duties].
v.c: He reigns supreme over all of His creation, and sends recording-angels, watching over you. When death comes to any of you, Our angels take their soul, never neglecting this duty.

q: are returned to Allaah, their True Master
and He is the fastest of those who take reckoning
v.s: Then they [i.e., His servants] are returned to God, their true Lord. Unquestionably, His is the judgement, and He is the swiftest of accountants.
v.c: Then they are ˹all˺ returned to Allah— their True Master. Judgment is His ˹alone˺. And He is the Swiftest Reckoner.

q: Say, “Who shall rescue you from the darkness of the land and sea when
to Him saying, 'Most surely if You save us from this
we will definitely be of the grateful ones
v.s: Say, "Who rescues you from the darknesses of the land and sea [when] you call upon Him imploring [aloud] and privately, 'If He should save us from this [crisis], we will surely be among the thankful.'"
v.c: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Who rescues you from the darkest times on land and at sea? He ˹alone˺ you call upon with humility, openly and secretly: “If You rescue us from this, we will be ever grateful.”

q: Say, “Allaah shall rescue you from it
(from the difficulty you find yourself in)
and from every other difficulty, yet you ascribe partners to Him!”
v.s: Say, "It is God who saves you from it and from every distress; then you [still] associate others with Him."
v.c: Say, “˹Only˺ Allah rescues you from this and any other distress, yet you associate others with Him ˹in worship˺.”

q: of sending to you a punishment from above
mixing you into various groups and then letting you taste each others brutality
(when you fight each other in war).”
See how We explain the Aayaat so that they understand
(the coming of the punishment or the Quraan).
v.s: Say, "He is the [one] Able to send upon you affliction from above you or from beneath your feet or to confuse you [so you become] sects and make you taste the violence of one another." Look how We diversify the signs that they might understand.
v.c: Say, “He ˹alone˺ has the power to unleash upon you a torment from above or below you or split you into ˹conflicting˺ factions and make you taste the violence of one another.” See how We vary the signs, so perhaps they will comprehend.

q: when it is the truth. Tell them, “I have not been put in charge of you
(to force you to do as I say. Just as the choice is yours, so too are the consequences).”
v.s: But your people have denied it while it is the truth. Say, "I am not over you a manager [i.e., authority]."
v.c: Still your people ˹O Prophet˺ have rejected this ˹Quran˺, although it is the truth. Say, “I am not a keeper over you.”

q: for every event and you shall soon come to know
(when the time of your punishment arrives. My duty is only to warn you).
v.s: For every news [i.e., happening] is a finality; and you are going to know.
v.c: Every ˹destined˺ matter has a ˹set˺ time to transpire. And you will soon come to know.

q: When you see those who engross themselves
then turn away from them until they engage in some other talk. Should Shaytaan cause you to forget
do not sit with the unjust people
v.s: And when you see those who engage in [offensive] discourse concerning Our verses, then turn away from them until they enter into another conversion. And if Satan should cause you to forget, then do not remain after the reminder with the wrongdoing people.
v.c: And when you come across those who ridicule Our revelations, do not sit with them unless they engage in a different topic. Should Satan make you forget, then once you remember, do not ˹continue to˺ sit with the wrongdoing people.

q: Those with Taqwa are not at all accountable for them
(for those who mock and find fault with the Aayaat of Allaah),
(it is their duty if they have the ability)
v.s: And those who fear God are not held accountable for them [i.e., the disbelievers] at all, but [only for] a reminder - that perhaps they will fear Him.
v.c: Those mindful ˹of Allah˺ will not be accountable for those ˹who ridicule it˺ whatsoever—their duty is to advise, so perhaps the ridiculers will abstain.

q: Leave those people alone who regard
and whom the worldly life has deceived. Use it
so that a soul is not detained
deeds. There shall neither be any helper nor intercessor for it
(to save itself from punishment in the Aakhirah),

it would not be accepted from it. These are the ones who have been detained because of their actions. They shall have a drink of boiling water and an unbearable punishment because they used to commit kufr.
v.s: And leave those who take their religion as amusement and diversion and whom the worldly life has deluded. But remind with it [i.e., the Qur’ān], lest a soul be given up to destruction for what it earned; it will have other than God no protector and no intercessor. And if it should offer every compensation, it would not be taken from it [i.e., that soul]. Those are the ones who are given to destruction for what they have earned. For them will be a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment because they used to disbelieve.
v.c: And leave those who take this faith ˹of Islam˺ as mere play and amusement and are deluded by ˹their˺ worldly life. Yet remind them by this ˹Quran˺, so no one should be ruined for their misdeeds. They will have no protector or intercessor other than Allah. Even if they were to offer every ˹possible˺ ransom, none will be accepted from them. Those are the ones who will be ruined for their misdeeds. They will have a boiling drink and painful punishment for their disbelief.

q: which can neither benefit us nor harm us and
Should we be like he whom Shaytaan had deviated from the path in a forest, leaving him bewildered
(confused and scared, unable to find his way)
when he has companions calling him to guidance
'Come to us!'?” Say, “Verily only the guidance of Allaah is
guidance and we have been commanded to surrender
to the Rabb of the universe,...
v.s: Say, "Shall we invoke instead of God that which neither benefits us nor harms us and be turned back on our heels after God has guided us? [We would then be] like one whom the devils enticed [to wander] upon the earth confused, [while] he has companions inviting him to guidance, [calling], 'Come to us.'" Say, "Indeed, the guidance of God is the [only] guidance; and we have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds.
v.c: Ask ˹them, O Prophet˺, “Should we invoke, other than Allah, those ˹idols˺ which cannot benefit or harm us, and turn back to disbelief after Allah has guided us? ˹If we do so, we will be˺ like those disoriented by devils in the wilderness, while their companions call them to guidance, ˹saying˺, ‘Come to us!’ Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Allah’s guidance is the ˹only˺ true guidance. And we are commanded to submit to the Lord of all worlds,

q: ...to establish salaah and to adopt Taqwa. He is the
One to Whom you will be
(for accountability on the Day of Qiyaamah).”
v.s: And to establish prayer and fear Him." And it is He to whom you will be gathered.
v.c: establish prayer, and be mindful of Him. To Him you will all be gathered together.

q: He is truly the One Who created the heavens and the earth.
The day when He shall say, “Be!” and it will be
(the Day of Qiyaamah, after which He will command people to rise from their graves and they will rise).
His speech is the truth and kingdom
shall be His on the day when the trumpet is blown. He is the Knower of the unseen and the visible and He is the Wise, the Informed.
v.s: And it is He who created the heavens and earth in truth. And the day [i.e., whenever] He says, “Be,” and it is, His word is the truth. And His is the dominion [on] the Day the Horn is blown. [He is] Knower of the unseen and the witnessed; and He is the Wise, the Acquainted.
v.c: He is the One Who created the heavens and the earth in truth. On the Day ˹of Judgment˺ He will say, ‘Be!’ And there will be! His command is truth. All authority is His ˹alone˺ on the Day the Trumpet will be blown. He is the Knower of all—seen or unseen. And He is the All-Wise, All-Aware.”

q: When Ibraheem ﵊ told his father Aazar, “Do you take idols
as your gods? I see that you and your people are certainly in manifest
v.s: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Abraham said to his father Āzar, “Do you take idols as deities? Indeed, I see you and your people to be in manifest error.”
v.c: And ˹remember˺ when Abraham said to his father, Ȃzar, “Do you take idols as gods? It is clear to me that you and your people are entirely misguided.”

q: (as We showed Ibraheem ﵊ the error of the ways of his people)
We showed Ibraheem ﵊ the kingdoms of the heavens and the earth so that
he could become of those convinced
(about the Oneness and greatness of Allaah and pass it on to others).
v.s: And thus did We show Abraham the realm of the heavens and the earth that he would be among the certain [in faith].
v.c: We also showed Abraham the wonders of the heavens and the earth, so he would be sure in faith.

q: When the night covered him, he saw a star. He said
“Can this be my Rabb?” But when it set
he said, “I do not like things that set
(because a Rabb cannot be absent when one needs Him).”
v.s: So when the night covered him [with darkness], he saw a star. He said, "This is my lord." But when it set, he said, "I like not those that set [i.e., disappear]."
v.c: When the night grew dark upon him, he saw a star and said, “This is my Lord!” But when it set, he said, “I do not love things that set.”

q: When he saw the moon shining, he said, “Can this be my Rabb?” But when it set, he said
“If my Rabb does not guide me I shall surely become of those who have gone astray.”
(By saying this, he indicated to the people that they were astray and in need of guidance.)
v.s: And when he saw the moon rising, he said, "This is my lord." But when it set, he said, "Unless my Lord guides me, I will surely be among the people gone astray."
v.c: Then when he saw the moon rising, he said, “This one is my Lord!” But when it disappeared, he said, “If my Lord does not guide me, I will certainly be one of the misguided people.”

q: When he saw the sun shining he said, “Can this
be my Rabb? This is the greater
But when it set he said, “O my people, indeed I am innocent of the things that you ascribe
v.s: And when he saw the sun rising, he said, "This is my lord; this is greater." But when it set, he said, "O my people, indeed I am free from what you associate with God.
v.c: Then when he saw the sun shining, he said, “This must be my Lord—it is the greatest!” But again when it set, he declared, “O my people! I totally reject whatever you associate ˹with Allah in worship˺.

q: to only that Being Who created the heavens and the earth, as a Haneef
(one who does not incline towards any deviation but inclines to the straight way, which is the path Allaah sanctions)
and I am not from the Mushrikeen.”
v.s: Indeed, I have turned my face [i.e., self] toward He who created the heavens and the earth, inclining toward truth, and I am not of those who associate others with God."
v.c: I have turned my face towards the One Who has originated the heavens and the earth—being upright—and I am not one of the polytheists.”

q: His people debated with him. He said, “Do you debate with me concerning
Allaah, when He has guided me
you ascribe as partner to Him,
(because they can do me no harm)
(to harm me, for then it most certainly will).
The knowledge of my Rabb surrounds everything
v.s: And his people argued with him. He said, "Do you argue with me concerning God while He has guided me? And I fear not what you associate with Him [and will not be harmed] unless my Lord should will something. My Lord encompasses all things in knowledge; then will you not remember?
v.c: And his people argued with him. He responded, “Are you arguing with me about Allah, while He has guided me? I am not afraid of whatever ˹idols˺ you associate with Him—˹none can harm me,˺ unless my Lord so wills. My Lord encompasses everything in ˹His˺ knowledge. Will you not be mindful?

q: “How can I fear that which you associate as partners
(to Allaah, which can neither do good not harm)
(the punishment that will afflict you because of the fact)
that you ascribe such partners to Allaah, regarding whom He has not revealed any permission
So which of the two groups
(If you have any knowledge, you would know that we are safe from Allaah's punishment because of our beliefs. You should therefore be following us.)
v.s: And how should I fear what you associate while you do not fear that you have associated with God that for which He has not sent down to you any authority? So which of the two parties has more right to security, if you should know?"
v.c: And how should I fear your associate-gods, while you have no fear in associating ˹others˺ with Allah—a practice He has never authorized? Which side has more right to security? ˹Tell me˺ if you really know!”

q: Those who have Imaan and do not mix their Imaan with wrong-doing
only such people will have safety
and only they are rightly guided.
v.s: They who believe and do not mix their belief with injustice - those will have security, and they are [rightly] guided.
v.c: It is ˹only˺ those who are faithful and do not tarnish their faith with falsehood who are guaranteed security and are ˹rightly˺ guided.

q: against his nation. We raise the stages of whoever We wish
(in respect of their knowledge and wisdom).
Verily your Rabb is the Wise, All Knowing.
v.s: And that was Our [conclusive] argument which We gave Abraham against his people. We raise by degrees whom We will. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing.
v.c: This was the argument We gave Abraham against his people. We elevate in rank whoever We please. Surely your Lord is All-Wise, All-Knowing.

q: Ya'qoob ﵊ both of whom We guided. We guided Nooh ﵊ before
Dawood ﵊, Sulaymaan ﵊, Ayyoob ﵊, Yusuf ﵊ Moosa ﵊ and Haroon ﵊. In this manner
We reward those who do good.
v.s: And We gave to him [i.e., Abraham] Isaac and Jacob - all [of them] We guided. And Noah, We guided before; and among his descendants, David and Solomon and Job and Joseph and Moses and Aaron. Thus do We reward the doers of good.
v.c: And We blessed him with Isaac and Jacob. We guided them all as We previously guided Noah and those among his descendants: David, Solomon, Job, Joseph, Moses, and Aaron. This is how We reward the good-doers.

q: Zakariyya ﵊, Yahya ﵊, Isa ﵊ and Ilyaas ﵊ all of whom were from the righteous
v.s: And Zechariah and John and Jesus and Elias - and all were of the righteous.
v.c: Likewise, ˹We guided˺ Zachariah, John, Jesus, and Elias, who were all of the righteous.

q: Ismaa'eel ﵊, Yasa ﵊, Yunus ﵊ and Loot ﵊. Each of them We favoured above the
v.s: And Ishmael and Elisha and Jonah and Lot - and all [of them] We preferred over the worlds.
v.c: ˹We also guided˺ Ishmael, Elisha, Jonah, and Lot, favouring each over other people ˹of their time˺.

q: And from their forefathers, progeny and brothers
(were many whom We guided and favoured by making them Ambiyaa as well).
We chose them and guided them to the straight path.
v.s: And [some] among their fathers and their descendants and their brothers - and We chose them and We guided them to a straight path.
v.c: And ˹We favoured˺ some of their forefathers, their descendants, and their brothers. We chose them and guided them to the Straight Path.

q: (Deen of islaam to which Allaah guided them)
is Allaah's guidance by which He guides whom He wills from His bondsmen. If
they commit Shirk, then all their actions will be destroyed
v.s: That is the guidance of God by which He guides whomever He wills of His servants. But if they had associated others with God, then worthless for them would be whatever they were doing.
v.c: This is Allah’s guidance with which He guides whoever He wills of His servants. Had they associated others with Him ˹in worship˺, their ˹good˺ deeds would have been wasted.

q: are the ones to whom We have granted the Book
wisdom and Prophethood. If the people of the present times reject this
(it will not harm us at all because)
people who will not reject it.
v.s: Those are the ones to whom We gave the Scripture and authority and prophethood. But if they [i.e., the disbelievers] deny it, then We have entrusted it to a people who are not therein disbelievers.
v.c: Those were the ones to whom We gave the Scripture, wisdom, and prophethood. But if these ˹pagans˺ disbelieve in this ˹message˺, then We have already entrusted it to a people who will never disbelieve in it.

q: are the people whom Allaah has guided, so follow their guidance
Say, “I do not ask you payment for it
(for the Qur'aan. If you reject it, the loss is your own while) I have nothing to lose).
It is but a reminder for the
v.s: Those are the ones whom God has guided, so from their guidance take an example. Say, "I ask of you for it [i.e., this message] no payment. It is not but a reminder for the worlds."
v.c: These ˹prophets˺ were ˹rightly˺ guided by Allah, so follow their guidance. Say, “I ask no reward of you for this ˹Quran˺—it is a reminder to the whole world.”

q: Allaah as they should have done when they said, “Allaah has not revealed anything to any human being.” Say
“Then who has revealed the Book that Moosa ﵊ brought as a light and guidance for people? You placed
it in various pages that you showed
but much of it you hid away
You were taught such things that neither you nor your forefathers had knowledge of.” Say
and then leave them to play their
(after you have preached the message to them, leave them to do as they please because your duty has been done).
v.s: And they did not appraise God with true appraisal when they said, "God did not reveal to a human being anything." Say, "Who revealed the Scripture that Moses brought as light and guidance to the people? You [Jews] make it into pages, disclosing [some of] it and concealing much. And you were taught that which you knew not - neither you nor your fathers." Say, "God [revealed it]." Then leave them in their [empty] discourse, amusing themselves.
v.c: And they have not shown Allah His proper reverence when they said, “Allah has revealed nothing to any human being.” Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Who then revealed the Book brought forth by Moses as a light and guidance for people, which you split into separate sheets—revealing some and hiding much? You have been taught ˹through this Quran˺ what neither you nor your forefathers knew.” Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Allah ˹revealed it˺!” Then leave them to amuse themselves with falsehood.

q: is the Book that We have revealed
which is most blessed, which confirms that
which was before it so that you may warn the people of “The Mother of all Villages”
Those who are convinced of the Aakhirah believe in it
(regularly, for they anxiously await the life after death).
v.s: And this is a Book which We have sent down, blessed and confirming what was before it, that you may warn the Mother of Cities [i.e., Makkah] and those around it. Those who believe in the Hereafter believe in it, and they are maintaining their prayers.
v.c: This is a blessed Book which We have revealed—confirming what came before it—so you may warn the Mother of Cities and everyone around it. Those who believe in the Hereafter ˹truly˺ believe in it and guard their prayers.

q: Who can be more unjust than he who invents lies about Allaah and says, “Revelation comes to me
when no revelation comes to him at all
says, “I shall soon reveal the same as that
which Allaah has revealed.” If only you could see the unjust ones in the pains
up your souls! Today you shall suffer a humiliating punishment because you used to speak lies about Allaah
and because you were too arrogant
to accept the Aayaat of Allaah.”
v.s: And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about God or says, "It has been inspired to me," while nothing has been inspired to him, and one who says, "I will reveal [something] like what God revealed." And if you could but see when the wrongdoers are in the overwhelming pangs of death while the angels extend their hands, [saying], "Discharge your souls! Today you will be awarded the punishment of [extreme] humiliation for what you used to say against God other than the truth and [that] you were, toward His verses, being arrogant."
v.c: Who does more wrong than the one who fabricates lies against Allah or claims, “I have received revelations!”—although nothing was revealed to them—or the one who says, “I can reveal the like of Allah’s revelations!”? If you ˹O Prophet˺ could only see the wrongdoers in the throes of death while the angels are stretching out their hands ˹saying˺, “Give up your souls! Today you will be rewarded with the torment of disgrace for telling lies about Allah and for being arrogant towards His revelations!”

q: (The Kuffaar will be told on the Day of Qiyaamah)
“Undoubtedly you have come to Us alone
as We created you the first time
and you have left behind your backs
We had blessed you with. We do not see
whom you claimed had a share in you
have been cut off and what you claimed
(that your idols will intercede for you)
v.s: [It will be said to them], "And you have certainly come to Us alone [i.e., individually] as We created you the first time, and you have left whatever We bestowed upon you behind you. And We do not see with you your 'intercessors' which you claimed that they were among you associates [of God]. It has [all] been severed between you, and lost from you is what you used to claim."
v.c: ˹Today˺ you have come back to Us all alone as We created you the first time —leaving behind everything We have provided you with. We do not see your intercessors with you—those you claimed were Allah’s partners ˹in worship˺. All your ties have been broken and all your claims have let you down.”

q: Undoubtedly Allaah is the One Who splits the seed and the date stone
(such as a chicken from an egg or a Mu'min from a Kaafir)
and the dead from the living
(such as an egg from a hen or a Kaafir from a Mu'min).
This is Allaah! So where are you wandering
v.s: Indeed, God is the cleaver of grain and date seeds. He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living. That is God; so how are you deluded?
v.c: Indeed, Allah is the One Who causes seeds and fruit stones to sprout. He brings forth the living from the dead and the dead from the living. That is Allah! How can you then be deluded ˹from the truth˺?

q: He causes the dawn to break, made the night a
rest and fixed orbits for the sun and the moon
This is the arrangement of The Mighty, The All Knowing.
v.s: [He is] the cleaver of daybreak and has made the night for rest and the sun and moon for calculation. That is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.
v.c: He causes the dawn to break, and has made the night for rest and ˹made˺ the sun and the moon ˹to travel˺ with precision. That is the design of the Almighty, All-Knowing.

q: It is He Who made the stars so that you may be guided by them
(so that you are able to find your route when you travel)
in the darkness of the land and
the ocean. Indeed We have explained the Aayaat
v.s: And it is He who placed for you the stars that you may be guided by them through the darknesses of the land and sea. We have detailed the signs for a people who know.
v.c: And He is the One Who has made the stars as your guide through the darkness of land and sea. We have already made the signs clear for people who know.

m: so (there is) a place of dwelling
q: It is He Who created you from a single soul
a place where you will stay
(for a longer period- Jannah or Jahannam)
and a place where you are kept in trust
(for a shorter period- the world/the grave).
Indeed We have clearly clarified the Aayaat for people who have intelligence
(who use their intelligence to ponder and think about Allaah's Aayaat).
v.s: And it is He who produced you from one soul and [gave you] a place of dwelling and of storage. We have detailed the signs for a people who understand.
v.c: And He is the One Who originated you all from a single soul, then assigned you a place to live and another to ˹be laid to˺ rest. We have already made the signs clear for people who comprehend.

q: from the sky, then by it
We bring forth grains that are stacked one on top of another
(with every one of these grains having the ability to grow into a complete plant bearing many more grains).
(a small stalk with little flowers enclosed in a leafy covering called a spathe)
of the date palm, We extract branches that hang low
(heavy because they are laden with dates)
Orchards of grapes, olives and pomegranates, some of which are alike
while others are not alike. Look at its fruit as it grows and ripens
(as it develops from something worthless into something valuable).
Indeed there are Aayaat in this for the people who have Imaan.
v.s: And it is He who sends down rain from the sky, and We produce thereby the growth of all things. We produce from it greenery from which We produce grains arranged in layers. And from the palm trees - of its emerging fruit are clusters hanging low. And [We produce] gardens of grapevines and olives and pomegranates, similar yet varied. Look at [each of] its fruit when it yields and [at] its ripening. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
v.c: And He is the One Who sends down rain from the sky—causing all kinds of plants to grow—producing green stalks from which We bring forth clustered grain. And from palm trees come clusters of dates hanging within reach. ˹There are˺ also gardens of grapevines, olives, and pomegranates, similar ˹in shape˺ but dissimilar ˹in taste˺. Look at their fruit as it yields and ripens! Indeed, in these are signs for people who believe.

q: (despite witnessing these signs of Allaah's power and greatness)
they regard the Jinn as partners to Allaah whereas He had created them
(How can creation be worshipped instead of the Creator?).
they invent sons and daughters for Him without knowledge
He is Pure from these things and Exalted above
v.s: But they have attributed to God partners - the jinn, while He has created them - and have fabricated for Him sons and daughters. Exalted is He and high above what they describe.
v.c: Yet they associate the jinn with Allah ˹in worship˺, even though He created them, and they falsely attribute to Him sons and daughters out of ignorance. Glorified and Exalted is He above what they claim!

q: How can He have children when He has no wife? He created everything and has knowledge of everything.
v.s: [He is] Originator of the heavens and the earth. How could He have a son when He does not have a companion [i.e., wife] and He created all things? And He is, of all things, Knowing.
v.c: ˹He is˺ the Originator of the heavens and earth. How could He have children when He has no mate? He created all things and has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of everything.

q: This Allaah is your Rabb! There is no Ilaah but Him, the Creator of all things, so worship Him
(for He Alone is worthy of worship).
v.s: That is God, your Lord; there is no deity except Him, the Creator of all things, so worship Him. And He is Disposer of all things.
v.c: That is Allah—your Lord! There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him. ˹He is˺ the Creator of all things, so worship Him ˹alone˺. And He is the Maintainer of everything.

q: cannot grasp Him, but He can grasp
(and can therefore not be seen in this world),
v.s: Vision perceives Him not, but He perceives [all] vision; and He is the Subtle, the Acquainted.
v.c: No vision can encompass Him, but He encompasses all vision. For He is the Most Subtle, All-Aware.

q: (with which man can understand Allaah's power)
have undoubtedly arrived from your Rabb. Whoever will
(the truth, to recognise Allaah and to bring Imaan),
is blind, it shall only be to his detriment
v.s: There has come to you enlightenment from your Lord. So whoever will see does so for [the benefit of] his soul, and whoever is blind [does harm] against it. And [say], "I am not a guardian over you."
v.c: Indeed, there have come to you insights from your Lord. So whoever chooses to see, it is for their own good. But whoever chooses to be blind, it is to their own loss. And I am not a keeper over you.

m: and that We (may) make it clear
q: (as We have explained everything else to you)
so that We may make it clear to those who have knowledge
v.s: And thus do We diversify the verses so they [i.e., the disbelievers] will say, "You have studied," and so We may make it [i.e., the Qur’ān] clear for a people who know.
v.c: And so We vary our signs to the extent that they will say, “You have studied ˹previous scriptures˺,” and We make this ˹Quran˺ clear for people who know.

q: Follow the revelation that your Rabb has sent to you.
(Remain steadfast on the most important belief of this revelation which is the fact that)
There is no Ilaah but Him. And
(because they will try to distract you from your objectives and because of their rejecting attitude).
v.s: Follow, [O Muhammad], what has been revealed to you from your Lord - there is no deity except Him - and turn away from those who associate others with God.
v.c: ˹O Prophet!˺ Follow what is revealed to you from your Lord—there is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him—and turn away from the polytheists.

q: (to Allaah). (However, their persistent Shirk should not grieve you, O Muhammad ﷺ because)
We have not made you a watcher
over them and you are not responsible for them
(your only responsibility is to convey the message of Islaam to them).
v.s: But if God had willed, they would not have associated. And We have not appointed you over them as a guardian, nor are you a manager over them.
v.c: Had Allah willed, they would not have been polytheists. We have not appointed you as their keeper, nor are you their maintainer.

q: worship instead of Allaah, for then they shall insult
Allaah out of enmity and without knowledge
(without realising the consequences of their actions).
(as We have made the gods of these people seem great to them)
the actions of every nation for them
(because of which they continue doing what they do).
they shall return to their Rabb and He will inform them of what they used to do
v.s: And do not insult those they invoke other than God, lest they insult God in enmity without knowledge. Thus We have made pleasing to every community their deeds. Then to their Lord is their return, and He will inform them about what they used to do.
v.c: ˹O believers!˺ Do not insult what they invoke besides Allah or they will insult Allah spitefully out of ignorance. This is how We have made each people’s deeds appealing to them. Then to their Lord is their return, and He will inform them of what they used to do.

q: swear earnest oaths by Allaah that if an Aayah
(a miracle that they desire, like turning Mount Safa into gold)
comes to them from Allaah, they will definitely accept Imaan. Say, “Aayaat
(a Nabi can only display a miracle when Allaah wills).”
(O Rasulullaah ﷺ, how can you be sure)
if they will accept Imaan when an Aayah
(Only Allaah knows whether they will accept Islaam by witnessing a miracle. It is therefore only He Who can decide whether they should be shown a miracle or not.)
v.s: And they swear by God their strongest oaths that if a sign came to them, they would surely believe in it. Say, "The signs are only with [i.e., from] God." And what will make you perceive that even if it [i.e., a sign] came, they would not believe.
v.c: They swear by Allah their most solemn oaths that if a sign were to come to them, they would certainly believe in it. Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Signs are only with Allah.” What will make you ˹believers˺ realize that even if a sign were to come to them, they still would not believe?

q: (so that they do no accept the truth)
(so that they do not see the truth)
just as they did not have Imaan the first time
(because they did not believe the first time)
v.s: And We will turn away their hearts and their eyes just as they refused to believe in it [i.e., the revelation] the first time. And We will leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly.
v.c: We turn their hearts and eyes away ˹from the truth˺ as they refused to believe at first, leaving them to wander blindly in their defiance.

q: Undoubtedly if We send the angels down to them
or if the dead speak to them
they are unlikely to accept Imaan
(they will become Mu'mineen only if Allaah wills).
However, most of them behave ignorantly
(by demanding to see miracles, knowing well that they have no interest in accepting Imaan but are only offering dishonest excuses).
v.s: And even if We had sent down to them the angels [with the message] and the dead spoke to them [of it] and We gathered together every [created] thing in front of them, they would not believe unless God should will. But most of them, [of that], are ignorant.
v.c: Even if We had sent them the angels, made the dead speak to them, and assembled before their own eyes every sign ˹they demanded˺, they still would not have believed— unless Allah so willed. But most of them are ignorant ˹of this˺.

q: (just as these people are your enemies, O Muhammad ﷺ)
We have appointed for every Nabi enemies
who are Shayaateen from among humans and Jinn. Some of them
deceive. If your Rabb wills, they will not do so
(However, Allaah allows this to take place for good reason).
(do not concern yourself with them because Allaah will deal with them as and when He wills).
v.s: And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy - devils from mankind and jinn, inspiring to one another decorative speech in delusion. But if your Lord had willed, they would not have done it, so leave them and that which they invent.
v.c: And so We have made for every prophet enemies—devilish humans and jinn—whispering to one another with elegant words of deception. Had it been your Lord’s Will, they would not have done such a thing. So leave them and their deceit,

m: and so that they may be pleased with it
and so that they may commit
q: So that the hearts of those who disbelieve in the Aakhirah are inclined to it
so that they grow fond of it
and so that they may engage in
(like following deceiving speech and worldly lusts)
(to cause further harm to the Prophets, their followers and their religion).
v.s: And [it is] so the hearts of those who disbelieve in the Hereafter will incline toward it [i.e., deceptive speech] and that they will be satisfied with it and that they will commit that which they are committing.
v.c: so that the hearts of those who disbelieve in the Hereafter may be receptive to it, be pleased with it, and be persistent in their evil pursuits.

q: (O Muhammad ﷺ, say to the Ahlul Kitaab, why)
Should I seek another judge besides Allaah
when He has revealed the Book
(distinctly making it clear to you that I am His Nabi because no man can ever compile such a masterpiece)?
Those to whom We have given the Book
is revealed with the truth from their Rabb, so do not ever become of the doubtful ones.
v.s: [Say], "Then is it other than God I should seek as judge while it is He who has revealed to you the Book [i.e., the Qur’ān] explained in detail?" And those to whom We [previously] gave the Scripture know that it is sent down from your Lord in truth, so never be among the doubters.
v.c: ˹Say, O Prophet,˺ “Should I seek a judge other than Allah while He is the One Who has revealed for you the Book ˹with the truth˺ perfectly explained?” Those who were given the Scripture know that it has been revealed ˹to you˺ from your Lord in truth. So do not be one of those who doubt.

q: There is none to alter His words and He is the All Hearing, the All Knowing.
v.s: And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and in justice. None can alter His words, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
v.c: The Word of your Lord has been perfected in truth and justice. None can change His Words. And He is the All-Hearing, All- Knowing.

q: If you follow the majority on earth
All they follow are their guesses
v.s: And if you obey most of those upon the earth, they will mislead you from the way of God. They follow not except assumption, and they are not but falsifying.
v.c: ˹O Prophet!˺ If you were to obey most of those on earth, they would lead you away from Allah’s Way. They follow nothing but assumptions and do nothing but lie.

q: Undoubtedly your Rabb knows best who has strayed from His path and He knows best who are the rightly guided ones
(He is therefore best able to judge between people).
v.s: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who strays from His way, and He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided.
v.c: Indeed, your Lord knows best who has strayed from His Way and who is ˹rightly˺ guided.

q: on which the name of Allaah was taken
v.s: So eat of that [meat] upon which the name of God has been mentioned, if you are believers in His verses [i.e., revealed law].
v.c: So eat only of what is slaughtered in Allah’s Name if you truly believe in His revelations.

q: What is the matter with you that you do not eat from that
on which Allaah's name was taken
when He has explained to you
(in many verses such as verse 145 of this Surah)
(for you to eat); (these things are Haraam)
which you are forced to eat
There are certainly many who, because of their
desires, lead others astray without knowledge
(without any reliable assurance to rely on). (However, they will not be able to escape without punishment because)
Undoubtedly your Rabb knows best those who over step the limits
(just as He know who the wrong-doers are).
v.s: And why should you not eat of that upon which the name of God has been mentioned while He has explained in detail to you what He has forbidden you, excepting that to which you are compelled. And indeed do many lead [others] astray through their [own] inclinations without knowledge. Indeed, your Lord - He is most knowing of the transgressors.
v.c: Why should you not eat of what is slaughtered in Allah’s Name when He has already explained to you what He has forbidden to you—except when compelled by necessity? Many ˹deviants˺ certainly mislead others by their whims out of ignorance. Surely your Lord knows the transgressors best.

q: sins. Certainly those who commit a sin will soon receive
the punishment for what they do.
v.s: And leave [i.e., desist from] what is apparent of sin and what is concealed thereof. Indeed, those who earn [blame for] sin will be recompensed for that which they used to commit.
v.c: Shun all sin—open and secret. Indeed, those who commit sin will be punished for what they earn.

m: so that they dispute with you
q: on which Allaah's name was not taken
is undoubtedly a sin. Without doubt, the Shayaateen whisper evil into the hearts of their friends
so that they dispute with you. If you follow them, you shall certainly be among the
v.s: And do not eat of that upon which the name of God has not been mentioned, for indeed, it is grave disobedience. And indeed do the devils inspire their allies [among men] to dispute with you. And if you were to obey them, indeed, you would be associators [of others with Him].
v.c: Do not eat of what is not slaughtered in Allah’s Name. For that would certainly be ˹an act of˺ disobedience. Surely the devils whisper to their ˹human˺ associates to argue with you. If you were to obey them, then you ˹too˺ would be polytheists.

q: then We granted to him life
by which he may walk among people
like him who is in a multitude of darkness
from which he will not come out
(as We have beautified Imaan for the Mu'mineen)
v.s: And is one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him light by which to walk among the people like one who is in darkness, never to emerge therefrom? Thus it has been made pleasing to the disbelievers that which they were doing.
v.c: Can those who had been dead, to whom We gave life and a light with which they can walk among people, be compared to those in complete darkness from which they can never emerge? That is how the misdeeds of the disbelievers have been made appealing to them.

q: (just as We have made the sinners, the prominent people of Makkah and the ringleaders, not too have)
We made the prominent ones in every town the sinners so that they may plot there
(to stop others from accepting Imaan and to involve them in sin).
(because they will be punished for it)
v.s: And thus We have placed within every city the greatest of its criminals to conspire therein. But they conspire not except against themselves, and they perceive [it] not.
v.c: And so We have placed in every society the most wicked to conspire in it. Yet they plot only against themselves, but they fail to perceive it.

q: (to prove that Rasulullaah ﷺ is Allaah's true Prophet)
say, “We will not accept Imaan until we are given what was given to the Rusul of Allaah
(unless revelation comes directly to us or we are given a complete scripture)!”
Allaah knows best where He wishes to place His message
(Allaah knows who qualifies to be His Rasool and where to send him).
punishment shall strike the sinful ones because of their plotting
v.s: And when a sign comes to them, they say, "Never will we believe until we are given like that which was given to the messengers of God." God is most knowing of where [i.e., with whom] He places His message. There will afflict those who committed crimes debasement before God and severe punishment for what they used to conspire.
v.c: Whenever a sign comes to them, they say, “We will never believe until we receive what Allah’s messengers received.” Allah knows best where to place His message. The wicked will soon be overwhelmed by humiliation from Allah and a severe punishment for their evil plots.

q: Whoever Allaah wishes to guide, He expands
(by placing the light of Imaan into it). (On the other hand,)
(by means of such sinful ideas so that it cannot accept Imaan)
(having great difficulty breathing because of a lack of oxygen).
(as such a person experienced great difficulty)
on those who do not have Imaan.
v.s: So whoever God wants to guide - He expands his breast to [contain] Islām; and whoever He wants to misguide - He makes his breast tight and constricted as though he were climbing into the sky. Thus does God place defilement upon those who do not believe.
v.c: Whoever Allah wills to guide, He opens their heart to Islam. But whoever He wills to leave astray, He makes their chest tight and constricted as if they were climbing up into the sky. This is how Allah dooms those who disbelieve.

q: is the straight path of your Rabb
(submission to Allaah and rejected false interpretation).
We have certainly clarified the Aayaat for those who will pay attention to the advice
v.s: And this is the path of your Lord, [leading] straight. We have detailed the verses for a people who remember.
v.c: That is your Lord’s Path—perfectly straight. We have already made the signs clear to those who are mindful.

q: Theirs shall be an abode of peace by their Rabb
v.s: For them will be the Home of Peace [i.e., Paradise] with their Lord. And He will be their protecting friend because of what they used to do.
v.c: They will have the Home of Peace with their Lord, Who will be their Guardian because of what they used to do.

q: The day when We shall gather them all
(all men and Jinn and then say),
“O assembly of Jinn! You certainly took a large group of humans
Then their human friends will say, “O our Rabb, we derived benefit from each other and
that You had fixed for us.” He
say, “Your abode will be the Fire, where you
shall live forever, except those whom Allaah wills
(that they should leave Jahannam after a while because of their Imaan. Such people will eventually enter Jannah).
Certainly your Rabb is The Wise, The All Knowing.”
v.s: And [mention, O Muhammad], the Day when He will gather them together [and say], “O company of jinn, you have [misled] many of mankind.” And their allies among mankind will say, “Our Lord, some of us made use of others, and we have [now] reached our term which You appointed for us.” He will say, “The Fire is your residence, wherein you will abide eternally, except for what God wills. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing.”
v.c: ˹Consider˺ the Day He will gather them ˹all˺ together and say, “O assembly of jinn! You misled humans in great numbers.” And their human associates will say, “Our Lord! We benefited from each other’s company, but now we have reached the term which You appointed for us.” ˹Then˺ He will say, “The Fire is your home, yours to stay in forever, except whoever Allah wills to spare.” Surely your Lord is All-Wise, All-Knowing.
v.h: Humans and Jinn on Judgment Day

q: (as We have made some humans the friends of some evil Jinn)
We make some of the oppressors companions of others because of the
(sinners committing the same sin will suffer the same punishment in the Aakhirah).
v.s: And thus will We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others for what they used to earn.
